title: Milestone sequencing & adaptive cut criteria for unified API / Console / Runtime launch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define a sequenced milestone plan and explicit, adaptive cut criteria for the coordinated launch of API, Console, and Runtime components. Goal is to minimize last-minute scope churn, surface high-risk regressions early, and provide deterministic guardrails for PM/Eng/Design/SRE during T-8 to T+2 weeks.

Scope: This ticket covers milestone definitions, scope-lock gating rules, progressive cut tiers (must-have / stretch / deferred), rollout guardrails, release notes ownership matrix, and stakeholder notification flows. It does NOT decide product-level pricing or external marketing content (those live in GTM-PRD).

Key deliverables (T-8w → T+1w):
- Milestone map with owners and acceptance criteria per milestone (alpha, beta, GA).
- Cut criteria matrix by risk axis (latency, correctness/regressions, security/compliance, infra capacity).
- Release notes choreography: who writes, who reviews, where to stage, and timeline for approvals.
- Communication plan and escalation path for scope rollback or emergent outages.
- Canary and rollout windows with automatic fallback triggers and metrics.

Milestone naming and intent:
- M0 (Scoping lock) — Outcome: final feature list and dependencies signed by PM/Eng/Design. Acceptance: Feature spec links, required infra capacity estimates, and known unknowns documented. Gate: >80% dependencies identified and triaged.
- M1 (Stability baseline) — Outcome: Feature branches merge to release candidate; automated e2e and perf tests passing on staging. Acceptance: Mean tail latency within target SLO on staging under representative load; no P0 regressions. Gate: Load test pass AND top 10 critical e2e smoke tests pass.
- M2 (Docs & Observability locked) — Outcome: Release notes drafted, console dashboards updated, tracing hooks enabled. Acceptance: Release notes drafted and reviewed; cost/latency dashboards show expected baselines. Gate: Docs and observability review complete.
- M3 (Canary & Ramp) — Outcome: Small % of traffic on production; rollback and fallback validated. Acceptance: Canary meets health metrics for 48 hours at target percent. Gate: Canary health pass.
- M4 (GA) — Outcome: Full traffic, public release notes live, support rotation ready. Acceptance: Incident playbooks reviewed; SLOs observed for 72 hours.

Adaptive cut criteria (principles):
1) Fail fast on customer-visible correctness regressions. Any semantic regression impacting >=1% of requests or a known customer path is P0 cut unless a clear mitigation exists.
2) Latency regressions tolerated up to incremental threshold (configurable per model family). Default cut if median latency increases >30% over baseline and tail increases >50% unless mitigations (batching knobs, autoscale) accepted.
3) Infra capacity shortfall: if Dedicated pool commitments cannot be met for predicted 95th percentile traffic, defer non-critical features (analytics exports, experimental quantization profiles) to post-GA.
4) Security/compliance: any failing security review or KMS integration regression is an immediate cut to resolve pre-GA.
5) Observability gaps: missing tracing or missing cost attribution for the release blocks GA or forces a reduced scope GA with an explicit re-evaluation date.

Release notes & documentation workflow:
- Owner: PM author drafts release notes (technical + customer-facing bullets) in docs/release_notes/DRAFT-<milestone>. Reviewers: Eng Lead, Design Lead, Support Lead, Legal (if feature collects data).
- Staging cadence: draft at M1, final at M2. Engineering provides a list of breaking changes and known limitations by M2. Marketing receives final copy at M3 for external comms.
- Changelog format: high-level intro (2-3 bullets), developer-facing changes (API/SDK signature changes), operational notes (SLO impact, rollout knobs), and migration steps.

Rollout and rollback triggers:
- Canary duration baseline: 48 hours at 5% traffic, then 24 hours at 25% if metrics stable.
- Automatic fallback: If canary error rate exceeds 1% absolute or 3x baseline, traffic is shifted to previous model/variant and alerts triggered.
- Manual rollback: PM+Tech Lead decision if persistent degradation >6 hours and no immediate mitigation.

Stakeholder matrix (initial):
- PM: Aisha Kapoor (owner) — milestone sign-off, release notes primary author.
- Eng Lead (Runtime): Priya Rao — performance acceptance and kernel/quantization gating.
- Eng Lead (API/Backend): Marcus Alvarez — API compatibility, throttling, rate-limiting.
- Design: Sofia Martinez — Console UI changes and release notes screenshots.
- SRE/Infra: Omar Patel — capacity validation, canary automation, SLIs.
- Support: Rachel Ng — runbook and triage readiness.

Open decisions & trade-offs:
- Decision needed: Allow feature-flagged experimental quantization profiles in GA release? Trade-off: potential cost improvements vs increased regression surface. Recommendation: move to M4 GA as opt-in after successful dedicated canary.
- Decision needed: Accept degraded observability for one optional metric to unblock docs shipping? Recommendation: Docs should not block GA unless metric is critical to rollback/rollback detection.

Success metrics for the launch:
- No critical regressions reported from top-10 customers in first 14 days.
- Production token latency within 10% of staging baseline at 95th percentile.
- Release notes published with migration steps and SDK examples before GA.
- Post-launch P0 incident count <=1 in first 30 days.

Notes: Links to artifact templates (release note template, canary playbook) are in attachments. Please add follow-up ticket keys to parent_issue if this ticket is split into multiple parallel tracks.
